title: 🧪 Mission — Test & Debug the Validator
subtitle: Write test cases against a password validator — and see if you can find a bug.
instructions: Replace each ??? with a real password to test. Write one VALID test, one INVALID test, and one EDGE CASE test. Think carefully about the edge case — it's the one most likely to reveal something interesting.
starterCode:
# TESTING & DEBUGGING - Morpheus Security Systems
# Mission: test this password validator and log your results

def validate(password):
    return len(password) > 8

# Step 1: Write 3 test cases below
# One VALID, one INVALID, and one EDGE CASE (think about the exact boundary!)

test1 = validate("???")
print(f"Test 1: validate(...) = {test1}")

test2 = validate("???")
print(f"Test 2: validate(...) = {test2}")

test3 = validate("???")
print(f"Test 3: validate(...) = {test3}")

# Step 2: Did one of your tests give a result you didn't expect?
# If so, you may have found a bug in validate() above — look closely
# at the comparison operator. Fix it, then re-run all three tests.
hints: A valid test: try a password you'd expect to pass, like a normal 10+ character password.
An invalid test: try something clearly too short, like a 3-character password.
An edge case: the task says 'at least 8 characters' — what happens with a password of EXACTLY 8 characters? Try it.
If your edge case gave a surprising result, check the comparison operator in validate() — is > the same as >=?

codeChecks.message: Complete Test 1 with a real password.
Complete Test 2 with a real password.
Complete Test 3 with a real password.

successMessage: Nice testing! If your edge case used exactly 8 characters, you should have found that validate() incorrectly rejects it. Did you spot that > should be >= ? Fix it and confirm all three tests now behave as expected. Ready for Silver? Write test cases for your Week 7 hashing/file storage functions too. Ready for Gold? Swap sandbox links with a partner and find a bug in each other's code.
